prompt:
A heavy trolley of mass 350 kg is pulled up a rough straight ramp inclined at 22.0 degrees to the horizontal by an electric winch cable parallel to the ramp. The trolley moves a distance of 45.0 m along the ramp at a steady speed. A constant frictional force of 220 N acts on the trolley opposing the motion.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Diagram showing a ramp of length 45.0 m inclined at 22.0 degrees to the horizontal. A trolley of mass 350 kg is on the ramp. A winch cable pulls the trolley up the slope with tension T. Opposing friction force 220 N acts down the slope parallel to the ramp. The vertical height gained is h.]
(a) Calculate the vertical height gained by the trolley. [1]
(b) Calculate the increase in gravitational potential energy of the trolley. [2]
(c) Calculate the work done against friction during the motion along the ramp. [1]
(d) Calculate the tension T in the winch cable. [2]

mark_scheme.criterion: Calculates vertical height Delta h = 45.0 * sin(22.0 deg) = 16.86 m (accept 16.9 m).
Uses Delta E_p = mg Delta h with m = 350 kg, g = 9.81 m s^-2, Delta h = 16.86 m.
Calculates Delta E_p = 5.79 * 10^4 J (or 57.9 kJ, accept 57.8 kJ to 58.0 kJ).
Calculates work done against friction W_f = F_f * s = 220 * 45.0 = 9.90 * 10^3 J (or 9900 J).
Uses conservation of energy W_total = Delta E_p + W_f = 57876 + 9900 = 67776 J, or resolves forces parallel to slope: T = mg sin(22.0 deg) + F_f.
Calculates tension T = W_total / s = 67776 / 45.0 = 1.51 * 10^3 N (or 1510 N).

marking_points.criterion: Calculates vertical height Delta h = 45.0 * sin(22.0 deg) = 16.86 m (accept 16.9 m).

part_enrichment.guidance: Use right-triangle trigonometry with the sine function: opposite = hypotenuse * sin(theta).
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Using cosine instead of sine, which calculates horizontal distance instead of vertical height.

marking_points.criterion: Substitutes values into Delta E_p = mg Delta h.

part_enrichment.guidance: Multiply mass (350 kg), g (9.81 m s^-2), and the vertical height gained (16.86 m).
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Using the slant distance of 45.0 m instead of the vertical height.

part_enrichment.guidance: Frictional force acts along the slope, so multiply the friction force directly by the distance moved along the slope.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Multiplying friction by vertical height rather than distance along the slope.

marking_points.criterion: Sets up total work equation or force balance parallel to the incline.

part_enrichment.guidance: At constant speed, total work done by winch equals GPE gained plus work against friction: W_total = 57876 + 9900 = 67776 J. Tension T = W_total / s = 67776 / 45.0 = 1506 N = 1.51 * 10^3 N. Alternatively, resolve forces parallel to the ramp: T = mg sin(22.0 deg) + 220 = 1286.3 + 220 = 1506.3 N.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Forgetting the friction component or forgetting the component of weight down the slope.

hints: In part (a), height is opposite to the angle of 22.0 degrees.
In part (b), apply Delta E_p = mg Delta h.
In part (c), work against friction is friction force multiplied by distance along the slope.
In part (d), at constant speed the tension does work equal to the sum of GPE gained and work against friction.
teacher_walkthrough: Step (a): Check right triangle trig: 45.0 sin(22 deg) = 16.86 m.
Step (d): Demonstrate both methods (energy balance and force resolution) to reinforce conceptual harmony.
Round all values to 3 significant figures.
